data.project_sub: Solace Home Goods (fictional test brand, not a real company) · 15s 9:16, 2 stills
data.title: Approve the full production package
data.ask: Approve the exact script, cast, looks, world, storyboard, sound plan and generation plan. Paid media still needs a separate budget.

strategy.proposition: The Solace pour-over is the five hands-on minutes you take back for yourself before the day takes the rest of your time — a small, repeatable act of choosing slow on purpose. (This operationalizes the brief's own key message, 'A five-minute ritual that slows your morning down, on purpose,' as a proposition the creative director can build routes against.)
strategy.tension: The target audience — urban professionals aged 25-40 who make coffee at home and say they value ritual over convenience — live inside schedules built for speed. For most of that group, coffee on a weekday is something you get (a pod, a drip machine on autopilot, a coffee-shop stop) rather than something you make. The tension is between wanting mornings to feel intentional and self-directed, and defaulting to whatever costs the least time, because deliberately slowing down can feel indulgent or impractical on a Tuesday. The brief names this tension directly by setting 'ritual' against 'convenience' as competing values, by pricing the product at $38 (a considered purchase, not an impulse one), and by warning against generic luxury imagery — the tension is not 'I want to look rich,' it's 'I want five minutes that are mine before the day takes them.'

routes.central_idea: Before the phone, the inbox, or anyone else gets a piece of you, there are five minutes that are only yours — marked by the pour.
routes.emotional_promise: Quiet self-possession: the felt relief of claiming a few minutes before the day starts claiming them for you.
routes.product_role: The Solace dripper is the literal boundary object. The film's one deliberate action — setting the phone face-down and reaching for the dripper instead — makes the product the mechanism of the choice, not a backdrop to it. It stays in frame through the pour, the bloom, and the final held mug, closing on an unhurried, fully lit shot of the dripper itself on the counter.
routes.execution_example: 15s / 9:16 (D01): Open tight on a phone screen lighting up on a counter; a hand turns it face-down without looking. Cut to the same hand lifting the Solace dripper, setting it on a mug, spooning grounds. Slow spiral pour, water blooming the grounds in close-up (2-3s held). Cut to the person at a window, mug in both hands, steam rising, a single distant notification sound goes unanswered. Final beat (2s): dripper alone on the counter in soft full light, product fully legible, with an illustrative closing line such as 'Made in small batches' (exact copy owned by copywriter). The two 4:5 stills (D02) pull directly from this beat structure: still 1 = the pour/bloom close-up with the dripper as clear hero object; still 2 = the closing counter shot, product fully visible and legible, doubling as a clean DTC-linkable product image.

routes.central_idea: The bloom itself — the moment water first meets the grounds — is the ritual's whole point, and the hand-glazed ceramic is filmed as the singular object that stages it.
routes.emotional_promise: Presence: the satisfaction of doing one small thing slowly enough to actually notice it happening.
routes.product_role: The dripper's surface and form are the visual subject, not just present in the shot. Macro texture on the hand-glazed stoneware (visible glaze variation, no two pieces identical) is used to make the tactile, handmade proof point legible on screen, then the frame pulls back to show the object in full use — giving the product both an intimate role and a clear closing moment.
routes.execution_example: 15s / 9:16 (D01): Near-entirely macro — dry grounds catching light, first pour, the bloom rising and settling, steam curling off the surface, a fingertip resting briefly on the glaze's texture. In the last 3 seconds, camera pulls back for the first time to a clean, fully lit shot of the dripper and finished mug on the counter, with a hand entering frame to lift the mug — the human presence and the product both land together as the closing moment. Illustrative closing line: 'Hand-glazed. Small batch. Yours.' The two 4:5 stills (D02) isolate: still 1 = the bloom macro shot; still 2 = the pulled-back closing counter shot, framed as a clean product/DTC image.

routes.central_idea: An ordinary Tuesday, not a weekend — the deliberate choice to reach for the slow thing instead of the fast thing, on a day that gave no permission to slow down.
routes.emotional_promise: Quiet agency: permission to choose slowness even when nothing about the day is asking for it.
routes.product_role: The dripper is staged as the chosen alternative in an explicit two-beat decision (reach for the fast option, then don't — reach for this instead), which makes its role in the story unmissable. It remains the visual anchor through the pour and into a final in-focus product shot.
routes.execution_example: 15s / 9:16 (D01): Opens on an out-of-focus stack of notifications/alarm on a phone, a hand starting to reach for it — then redirects to the Solace dripper sitting on the counter instead. One continuous, steady pour; the frame holds on the bloom. Final beat: person seated, mug in both hands, dripper still visible in soft foreground focus. On-screen line (illustrative, copywriter to finalize): 'A five-minute ritual, on purpose.' The two 4:5 stills (D02): still 1 = the redirected-hand moment (phone out of focus behind, dripper sharp in the foreground) carrying the tension itself; still 2 = the seated closing shot with the product legible in frame.

data.recommendation: R1 ("the line before the day") most directly dramatizes the strategy's own audience tension — ritual vs. the pull of convenience — through one specific, small, believable action (turning the phone face-down) rather than a generic mood board or an explicit before/after contrast edit. That keeps it furthest from the brief's 'generic luxury imagery without a story' risk while still giving the product an unambiguous role and a clean, legible closing shot that doubles easily as a DTC-linkable image. Its single continuous pace (no hard tonal cut) also fits the brief's 'quiet, warm, tactile' tone more precisely than R3's two-beat contrast, and it extends more naturally to both required still crops than R2's mostly-macro treatment, which risks losing legible product context if used as a static image on its own. R2 and R3 remain strong alternates: R2 is the more sensory, tactile-proof-point-forward option if the brand wants to foreground the hand-glazed/small-batch facts even more literally; R3 is the more literal, message-forward option if the producer wants the 'on purpose' contrast made explicit rather than implied.

panel.ended: below A after 3 rounds; the open notes are listed for Lucas

lenses.verdict: Not today, but close. The idea works. A phone flipped face-down at 7:00, a second buzz that shows up as rings in her coffee and gets nothing from her hand, and 'Everyone else gets you at 7:05.' That is dry, ownable execution. Every department serves R1, the product is a tool before it is the hero, and the taste notes are followed or broken on purpose with reasons. What stops approval is that the package doesn't agree with itself. Sound is timed to a superseded camera plan: six hits are off, and the turn's buzz trails its own picture. The treatment still carries the 18f/54f SH02A/SH02B split and wall-D card placements the camera plan can't honour. The camera plan contradicts the script's 7:05 card frame. The world bible drains away the drop the B4a beat needs. Two route departures (locked camera, neutral DTC still) wait on Lucas. I'd also cut the B2 card, so the thumb pass and the product's first look play without text and 7:05 lands as the only line. Make these fixes, get the real sample and Lucas's calls, and this goes to the client as an A.

Rewrite S1 to: SH02A 1.50-2.50 s (24f), with the hook at 0-6f, the thumb sweep at 6-14f and the lift at 14-24f; SH02B 2.50-4.50 s (48f), opening 12 cm short of the mug, with the click on SH02B f14 (3.08 s, absolute f74). notes.note: Replace the wall-D card-area placement with the camera plan's on-screen zones, which are the only ones inside the platform safe band: B4b on bare oak at 54-64% h below the dripper foot; B5-B6 on bare oak at 50-64% h, 8-84% w; the SH05 fallback on wall-D paint at 15-21% h. B2's zone only applies if the copywriter keeps the B2 card. Close camera plan blocker 3.

notes.target: D01-B2 on_screen_text 'Nobody gets you before the pour.'
notes.note: Cut this card from D01 and keep the line as the D02-1 headline. It lands on the same frame as the product's first look and the SH02A thumb pass, the only in-use demonstration of 'hand-glazed', and the treatment already flags that it pulls the eye. It also says in words what the B1 flip has just shown, and it takes the construction the 7:05 card pays off. Cutting it brings on-screen text from 8.5 s to 5.5 s of the 15, and 7:05 becomes the spot's only story line. If the sound-off phone test shows the read fails without it, the only allowed fallback is in at the SH02B cut (2.50 s) and out at 4.50 s (32 characters in 2.0 s, 16 cps). It never runs over SH02A.

notes.target: D01-B6 organic alternate card 'Shop the Solace dripper. Link in bio.'
notes.note: Trim it to 'Shop the dripper. Link in bio.' That is 30 characters in 2.0 s (15 cps), down from 37 (18.5 cps), and it would otherwise be the fastest card in the spot on the loop frame. The 'Solace' sign-off beneath it already names the brand. The paid card stays as written.

notes.target: camera_plan SH05 action: 'By about 30f (9.75 s) the rings are flat as the card comes up'
notes.note: Conform the action to the script. The 7:05 card comes up at SH05 24f (9.50 s), on the frame the rattle stops and the rings begin to flatten, and the rings are flat by about 30f with the card already up. Put the card-in frame in the action line so the editor and the sound designer work from one frame.

notes.target: camera_plan SH01 framing marks list ('ring 232.7/280'), SH04 ('Dripper on the ring'), SH07 ('the ring is clean oak'), SH08 ('the foot is on the ring mark')
notes.note: Rename every instance to 'set-down mark 232.7/280 (clean oak)'. 'Ring' is left over from the cut Mark 1 stain. A dressing or generation pass that reads it could add a coffee ring under the foot on the DTC image.

notes.target: world_bible PROP-01 persistent_state_notes ST4: 'Props drain the cone before the take, so nothing else drips.'
notes.note: Amend ST4 to match the treatment. Props let the cone drain until drips slow to about one a second, then roll so the lift comes 0.5-0.8 s after the last drip, so one drop hangs at the exit hole when SH04 rolls. Pass: that drop falls into the coffee within 7.17-7.42 s in at least one take in three, and nothing drips during the 15 cm carry. State the fallback too: if it fails, the drop falls during the 3 cm lift.

notes.target: world_bible PROP-01 description and product_placement 'Swap test ... It is the only swap test.'
notes.note: Write the script's hero-unit fallback into the bible now, with position and bearing: if the real unit has no foot pool, the swap-test detail is the iron speck and the thin glaze break at the rim. Give the arc of rim the D01-B2 thumb crosses, its bearing (235°, facing the lens in D01-B5/B6 and D02-2), and its tone against the body. The generation plan's checks then cite a named detail rather than 'the production designer's replacement'.

notes.target: world_bible LOC-01 spatial_layout: 'Coffee mirror line' paragraph, the FAUCET-01 rule 'Any frame that shows y < 185 needs FAUCET-01 built', and product_placement 'Mirror path, in section and plan'
notes.note: (1) Cut the lens-dependent maths (the coffee mirror-line formula in h and d, and the pool mirror path by lens elevation θ) and keep only set facts: coffee surface at 98.5 cm, TILE-01 edges at 112.0 and 119.5 cm, which flats are built for reflections, and the gloss finishes. The camera plan already carries its own mirror points. (2) Restate the faucet rule as 'any frame that shows FAUCET-01 at 254/155 needs it built'. Record that SH02A's corner, about 7 cm into the dry, empty sink at y≈178 with the faucet out of frame, meets the rule, which closes camera plan blocker 7.

notes.target: casting_bible visual_identity_anchors skin line ('These words go with the hex codes into the hand-double call and every prompt'), blocker 1 (generated NORA) and blocker 3 (grip)
notes.note: (1) Change the skin line to: words go in prompts; hex codes go only in the hand-double call and the acceptance checks. (2) Mark blocker 1 moot, because the generation plan has zero generated jobs, and reopen it only if a generated fallback is ever planned. (3) Record the director's named grips in blocker 3. In B2 the index and middle fingers hook over the rim with the thumb outside; in B4a it is a claw over the rim. So the threshold is set on rim diameter: 10.5 cm or more, or casting reopens the hand breadth.

notes.target: style_bible hair_makeup 'CHECK AND REAPPLY at the start of each hand setup (D01-B1, B2, B4a, B4b, D02-1)' and the assumption 'I don't know which hand appears in D01-B1, B2, B4a and B4b'
notes.note: Key the checks to the camera plan's shot IDs. The right hand (mole) is in SH01, SH02A, SH02B and SH04-SH05 (one take, one check before it). The left hand (scar) is in SH07. SH03 is the left-hand pour off frame, so re-check the scar after SH03 and before SH07, because water and steam contact trigger a reapply. Delete the 'don't know which hand' assumption.

notes.target: storyboard sound_cues in SH02A, SH02B, SH03, SH04 and SH05; on_screen_text in SH02A/SH02B and SH05
notes.note: Once the sound plan is re-synced, re-board every cue line at the corrected in-shot frames. Drop the '(see SYNC)' tags and move SYNC to CLOSED THIS ROUND. If the copywriter cuts the B2 card, clear the SH02A and SH02B on_screen_text and the 'card lands in the top band' language from both board notes. Set the SH05 card-in to the frame the cinematographer conforms to.

notes.target: generation_plan SH02A-PLT, SH06-PLT and SH08-STL acceptance checks: 'the production designer's replacement swap-test detail'
notes.note: Once the world bible names the fallback, cite it by name in all three jobs: iron speck and rim glaze break at 235°. Set a measurable read for it, at least 40 px at 100% on a 6-inch phone, the same bar as the pool. In SH02A-PLT, state that the thumb crosses the rim break on the lens side without stopping.

lenses.verdict: This is a strong, unusually specific package built on an idea the brand can own. The day's second buzz reaches her coffee as rings and gets nothing back, and the 7:00 to 7:05 window turns the key message into picture and cards without a spoken word. The claims discipline is clean, with only the three verified facts on screen. I would not shoot it next week as it stands. The sound plan is synced to a superseded camera plan, with six hits off by 5-17 frames. The treatment still carries old timings and a card area the camera can't see. The SH01 grip can't physically land the phone against the mug the way QC requires. SH07's locks already fail on paper. The turn depends on rings in a 1.2 cm patch of coffee. A person also has to decide several things before anything is locked: the real product sample, the two route departures, the hand-double release and whether we build or go to a location. With the 17 notes above made and those calls in, this is an A.

notes.target: sound_cues lines in SH02A, SH02B, SH03, SH04, SH05; the SYNC flag

notes.target: on_screen_text in SH02A, SH02B, SH05, SH06, SH07, SH08
notes.note:
Add a super spec for every card, because nothing in the package sets type size or colour. For each card give the typeface class, the minimum cap height in px on the 1080-wide frame (sized to read at 100% on a 6-inch phone within its hold), the colour, and the measured contrast against the surface it sits on:
- B2: on TILE-01 #D5D8D2, with grout lines. Dark type.
- B4b, B5 and B6: on oak #533C2B. Light type.
- D02-1: on oak.
- D02-2: on paint #6B6E67.
The cards carry the whole story for muted viewers.

notes.target: TILE-01 extent on wall D
notes.note: Extend the tile course from y 250 toward wall A, keeping the same 112.0-119.5 cm heights, until the bullnose end sits outside SH02A's right frame edge (plan estimate y≈215; confirm at prelight). The B2 card then sits on one continuous pale band in both angles. At the moment it crosses the bullnose onto dark paint in SH02A. The heights do not change, so SH05's coffee mirror line (y 318-327) is untouched.

notes.target: PROP-01 ST4 persistent_state_notes
notes.note: Replace 'Props drain the cone before the take, so nothing else drips' with the treatment's procedure: let the cone drain until drips slow to about one a second, then roll so the lift comes 0.5-0.8 s after the last drip. Wipe any drop that falls inside the foot ring at the SH06 reset. Pass: in at least one take in three, a single drop falls into the coffee within SH04 4-10f, and no second drop falls during the carry. As written, the bible removes the drop the script's B4a depends on.

notes.target: PROP-03 ST4 (SH04-SH05 hand takes)
notes.note: Set a working temperature for the mug in the hand takes. Fill so the mug's outer wall, where the fingertips rest (225-315° below the rim), reads at most 50°C on an IR thermometer at roll, while the coffee still shows thin steam in the raking key. Re-fill between takes to that number and log it. As written, the double rests dead-still fingertips on a freshly brewed diner mug for up to 4.5 s per take across many takes. That is a flinch and burn risk aimed straight at the beat's 'no flinch, no squeeze'.

notes.target: LOC-01 FAUCET-01 build rule; camera plan blocker 7
notes.note: Restate the rule by what a frame actually sees: FAUCET-01 is built only if a frame sees the faucet's footprint (about 254/155), not whenever y<185 shows. Confirm that SH02A's bottom-right corner shows about 7 cm of dry, empty sink with the faucet out of frame, and close camera plan blocker 7.

notes.target: Treatment S1 and S3: action_progression timings and card placement in blocking
notes.note:
Rule on the camera plan's open items and conform the treatment:
- SH02A/SH02B: accept 24f / 48f with the seat on SH02B 14f (3.08 s). Replace '18 f', 'f1-6/f7-14/f15-18' and 'SH02B 54 f, seat on f15'.
- SH04: accept the 4/2/14/5/11 split and replace '4/4/10/6/12'. A 21 cm arc in 10f peaks near 0.8 m/s.
- Cards: in S1 and S3 blocking, strike 'the world bible's bare card area (wall-D paint, 125 cm up)'. Adopt the camera plan's on-screen zones: B2 at 16-26% h; B4b and B5-B6 on bare oak.

notes.target: SH01 grip (ruling 9) in treatment S1 action_progression
notes.note:
The written grip cannot finish the way the acceptance check requires. The thumb starts on the wall-C long edge and the fingertips on the mug-side edge. A 180° roll about the long axis swaps the edges, so the thumb ends up between the phone and the mug, and the phone cannot then land touching the mug 'with no finger between'. Re-block it:
- During the roll, the thumb slides onto the back plate, so the hand finishes palm-down with the fingers on the wall-C edge.
- The hand lowers the free mug-side edge against the mug and opens.
- Rehearse this at the fitting.
If it won't play at habit speed, accept a landing gap of up to 1 cm in SH01, and have props close the phone to contact across the SH01/SH02A walk ellipsis. B4b is a separate setup.

notes.target: Ruling 4 / SH05 plan of record
notes.note: Make C4' the plan of record for SH05: the tighter frame, with the coffee at about 2.0 × 0.9 cm on a 6-inch screen and the dripper whole, cut from SH04 at the settle (8.5 s). Keep the 42 cm single take only as an upgrade if the ring test passes at phone size. At 42 cm the coffee is 1.2 × 0.7 cm, and the whole sound-off turn depends on it.

notes.target: Treatment S2 blocking for D02-1 (SH07)
notes.note: Drop 'cropped to include the index finger's middle joint so the scar reads'. L's fingertips on the beech handle stay in frame only as far as the lock keeping the sill out and the scorch band allow. Every plate uses the same practical double and nothing is generated, so the scar does no continuity work on screen. Run the mirror check from a wider safety frame at the same setup. This removes a conflict the plan's first estimate already fails (scar joint at 2-4% w against the 6% lock).

notes.target: SH01, SH04, SH05 lighting
notes.note: Say how the hand separates from the counter. Skin #6F4A34 (L* 35) sits only about 8 L* above the #533C2B oak, and nothing in the plan lifts it. Specify a named edge, for example the WIN-01 key's back-edge rim along the knuckles and the top of the forearm, at least +1 stop over the adjacent oak. Add a monitor check that the hand's outline reads at 100% on a 6-inch phone, especially in SH05, where the heel rests on the oak.

Two edits:

notes.note: Cut 'Shop the Solace dripper. Link in bio.' (37 characters in 2.0 s, 18.5 cps) to 31 characters or fewer so it reads at the spot's own ceiling, for example 'Shop the dripper. Link in bio.' (30 characters). The 'Solace' sign-off beneath already names the brand, and the verb stays.

notes.target: D01-B1 and D01-B4b picture/sound lines

Conform two timings to the camera and sound plans:

- B4b: 'about 1.0s long' and 'About 1.0s in, the rattle stops' become about 0.8 s (8.7-9.5 s).

notes.target: casting_bible blockers and the left-hand-pour rationale in assumptions
notes.note:
Four updates:
- Close 'Rights for a generated NORA'. Every plate is practical and nothing is generated, so what remains folds into the hand-double release.
- Update the dimensions/grip blocker. The director has named both grips (rim hook in B2, claw over the rim in B4a). Both cross the rim, so the threshold is the rim diameter: 11.5 cm assumed against the 10.5 cm minimum, pending the real unit.
- Strike 'because of where the kettle lives'. RANGE-01's burner at 212/97 is on her right (she faces 90° at y 308), so she fetches the kettle with R and switches it to L across the S1/S2 ellipsis. Say that instead.
- Align the skin-anchor line ('with the hex codes into every prompt') with the style bible's words-only rule.

notes.target: SH03-PLT acceptance_checks (continuity line)
notes.note: Replace 'At exit the grounds are a wet dome about 1 cm high' with the treatment's pass mark: by 2.2 s in-shot (6.7 s) the whole visible bed has darkened and the centre has visibly risen by at least 5 mm, judged at 100% on a 6-inch phone. 1 cm is the target, not the pass. As written, a take the director would pass fails QC.

lenses.verdict: The idea sells. Refusing the phone before the pour, the day's buzz reaching the coffee and nothing further, and the lines 'Everyone else gets you at 7:05' and 'Out from 7:00. Back at 7:05' are specific and relatable to our audience. The spot stays strictly inside our three facts and ends on a readable 3.5 s product hold with a clear CTA. I can't approve it for production today, for four reasons. The product's look, including the glaze pool the whole swap test rests on, is invented until we supply a real unit. The sound plan is synced to a camera plan that has been replaced. Three timing and placement rulings are still open. And the route departures and releases need decisions only people can make. Fix the notes above and answer the questions, and this is an 8 heading to a 9.

script.idea_in_one_line: At 7:00 the phone goes face-down and the dripper comes up. The next buzz reaches her coffee but not her, and nobody gets her until 7:05.
script.cta: Shop the Solace dripper. (Paid, primary: the platform's Shop Now button carries the DTC product-page link. Organic alternate card: 'Shop the Solace dripper. Link in bio.')

beats.picture: HOOK. A phone lies face-up on an oak counter with a chipped white mug right beside it. The lock screen lights: 7:00 in large readable digits, with one generic notification banner beneath it, its text too small to read. It buzzes. At about 0.8s NORA's hand comes in. The hand doesn't slow: it flips the phone in passing, the phone's edge lands against the mug, and the hand carries straight on right, toward the rack.
beats.sound: One phone buzz rattling on the counter, then the soft knock of the case landing on wood. Then silence.

beats.picture: Two angles. First angle: the same hand lifts the Solace dripper out of the dish rack. As the hand closes on it, the thumb passes over the glaze pooled unevenly at its foot without stopping, the mark B5 later turns to the lens. The hand sets off low and level. Cut mid-carry: the dripper comes in right to left and seats with a click on the chipped white mug, which still touches the face-down phone's edge. The hand lets go and stays clear of the phone. B2 ends on the empty dripper sitting on the mug. The card sits clear of the dripper in both angles.
beats.sound: A faint knock as the dripper leaves the dish rack; room tone across the cut; stoneware clicking onto the mug rim.
beats.text: Nobody gets you before the pour.

beats.picture: Cut to grounds already heaped in a pressed paper filter inside the Solace dripper. A gooseneck spout comes in from frame left and pours a slow spiral onto them. The grounds swell, bubble and dome up against the paper. Hold on the bloom to the end of the beat.
beats.sound: A thin stream of water on wet grounds; the soft fizz of the bloom. No music.

beats.picture: NORA's hand lifts the Solace dripper off the chipped mug, and a last drip falls from its tip into the coffee. The hand sets the dripper down on the oak counter just past the mug, on the side away from the phone, so the three sit in a line: phone, mug, dripper. The coffee's surface is now open to the lens.
beats.sound: A last drip plinking into the coffee; stoneware set down on wood.

beats.picture: Phone, mug and dripper in a line on the oak counter. NORA's fingertips rest along the chipped mug's side below the rim, palm clear, the heel of her hand on the counter. The mug touches the face-down phone's edge. The Solace dripper stands just past the mug, on the side away from the phone, in frame for the whole beat. The phone rattles against the wood and the coffee shivers into fine rings. About 1.0s in, the rattle stops, the rings flatten, and her hand stays where it is. The card comes up at 9.5s as the rings flatten, holds to 11.5s, and sits clear of the dripper.
beats.sound: One phone buzz, about 1.0s long, rattling against the wood and ticking against the mug, left unanswered. It stops. Room tone.

beats.picture: Moments later the mug and hand are gone. The Solace dripper stands empty on the oak counter with its filter out. The glaze pooled unevenly at its foot, the mark her thumb crossed in B2, faces the lens. At the frame edge, clear of the dripper, the phone lies face-down and dark. The whole product is in frame and legible.
beats.sound: Room tone; off screen, the kettle ticking as it cools.

beats.picture: The B5 frame, held. The empty Solace dripper stands on the oak counter with the glaze pooled at its foot facing the lens, and the phone lies face-down and dark at the frame edge. The whole product is legible. Nothing in frame moves.
beats.sound: Room tone and the kettle ticking as it cools, to the last frame. No music, no sting.

cast.role: Principal and the only person on screen. She appears as hands and forearms only, seen in D01-B1, B2, B4a, B4b and D02-1. B3 shows only the spout. The script sets her name and gender. Habit: every weekday at 7:00 she makes the pour before anyone else gets any of her. Backstory, not a lock: she keeps her lists on paper rather than in the phone, which gives her a writer's callus on the right middle finger. It adds no prop, scene or copy. Playable objective: get the coffee poured and her fingertips on the mug while the phone gets nothing back from her. Age: playing 33-39, target 36. This is a choice, not a story need. It sits inside the 25-40 audience, it is old enough for the habit to look long-standing, and it reads in the creased knuckles. Heritage: not specified. The skin value is the casting choice, and a hand double is matched on the anchors, not on heritage. Defaults broken: the category's default hand is late-20s, pale and slim, with a gloss manicure and stacked gold rings on a linen cuff. The generator's stock hand is long, tapered, poreless and light-skinned. I break both because 'Hands before faces' only works if the hand isn't stock. A stock hand also drifts toward the generic luxury imagery the brief rules out.
cast.presence: One-frame read: a broad, square hand in its mid-thirties, with medium-deep skin, a warm undertone (#6F4A34), creased knuckles and short bare nails. Two raised veins run from the wrist across the back of each hand. They are age texture and are not locked, because heat and hand height change them. The hand flips the buzzing phone face-down in passing, without looking, and is already moving on toward the rack. The hand never searches or hovers: it lands on an object, takes it and lets go. It lifts the dripper out of the rack the way it would lift a mug it uses every day, and the thumb crosses the pooled glaze at the foot without stopping. During the pour the forearm stays still and only the wrist circles. Between actions the hand stops completely: it lies flat and doesn't tap. On the mug, the fingertips touch it without gripping it, and they stay there. Conclusion earned: this hand has done this every morning for years.
